The four matcher constructions differ by which ignore file they read and by what each absence means, and folding them into one helper would scatter that per-file handling, so the flat sequence is the clearest available form.

adjudication.criterion: A finding is a true positive when the flagged site should actually be changed, judged at the pinned revision under the published scope of the rule; it is a false positive when the flagged construct is correct as written, when its safety is established by the surrounding code, or when the context makes the flagged behaviour the intended one. Confirming that the rule's pattern is present is a separate, mechanical check: it proves the span is not corrupted, never that the site is a defect. For structural findings the value question is stated separately. A duplication family is a true positive when its members repeat a nontrivial shared scaffold that one definition, parameter or macro could serve without changing behavior; it is a false positive when the shared body is a short delegation whose entire difference lives in the erased names, when the members mirror each other by design, as benchmark or test comparison pairs and replays under a different harness do, or when separate trait impls the language forces apart leave nothing to factor. A complexity or size hotspot is a true positive when decomposition is feasible and would plausibly be accepted, a false positive when the measured branch count or length is the clearest available form or is forced by a trait contract. An unreasoned allow or an unreferenced feature is a false positive when the surrounding code or manifest already documents the intent the detector could not read.
adjudication.provenance: Who produced each verdict. "human" names a site a person read and judged. "agent" names a site adjudicated by an agent under the published protocol: the site read in the pinned source with its surrounding code, blind to any prior verdict, with a disagreement between independent passes escalated rather than settled by the agent. "unrecorded" names the sites judged before this field existed, whose author is not established; they are published as they were measured rather than reattributed after the fact. A rate mixing provenances is worth its weakest one, and no verdict, whoever produced it, is certified beyond the agreement two trained reviewers reach with each other.

movepicker.rs stacks four independent units plus tests: the History tables with their bonus and aging math (lines 21 to 186), the staged MovePicker itself (188 to 920), a 200-line is_pseudo_legal validator that touches no picker state, QMovePicker (1180 to 1326), and six separate test modules from line 1327 on. History and is_pseudo_legal are natural sibling files.

export_html interleaves three separable things in one body: an 85-line CSS raw-string literal, a 30-line navigation JavaScript raw-string literal, and the per-slide render loop whose six sections (title/subtitle, bullets, code blocks, block quotes, tables, image data-URI, notes) each push into the same String. Hoisting the two literals to consts and lifting the loop body to fn render_slide(&Slide) -> String leaves the entry point at roughly forty lines with no behavior change, since the only shared state is the html accumulator. Nothing here is forced by a trait contract; escape_html already sits beside it as a free helper.

apply_font_change bundles two independent strategies plus a resize drain: the slide path builds a full-screen buffer, computes Kitty font stepping parameters, and runs a dissolve loop nested five levels deep (frame, row, span, char, cell padding) while interleaving font step batches, and the plain path then switches on font_capability. The dissolve frame renderer alone is an obvious extraction.

create_tpcc_schema_vibesql is nine consecutive db.create_table(TableSchema::with_primary_key(...)).unwrap() statements for warehouse, district, customer, history, new_order, orders, order_line, item and stock, with no branching, no loop and no state beyond the varchar() closure. The length is the arity of the TPC-C schema itself, about ninety ColumnSchema::new lines whose column names and types all differ, so there is nothing to factor and a split into nine single-statement functions would add indirection without removing anything. The flat declarative sequence is the clearest form and matches the sibling MySQL schema function in the same file.

The TableSchema impl runs 45 methods across four unrelated groups: six with_* builder constructors (with_primary_key through with_all_constraint_types), read accessors (get_column, column_count, primary_key_effective_collations), column mutations (add_column, remove_column, rename_column, set_column_nullable, set_column_default), and constraint mutations (add and drop for check, unique and foreign key). Splitting into per-concern impl blocks changes no call site.

process_constraints is two independent phases against one accumulator: the column-level loop matching ColumnConstraintKind over roughly a hundred and ten lines, then the table-level loop matching TableConstraintKind over sixty-five, sharing only `result` and the has_column_level_pk flag that the first phase alone owns. Each phase extracts to a function taking table_name, columns and &mut ConstraintResult, and each keeps its own exhaustive match, so no compile-time coverage is lost. The file already hosts free helpers of that shape next door: dedup_pk_key_parts, key_part_collations and validate_check_expression.

check_child_references_impl is two phases joined by one vector: a 140-line collection loop over every catalog table and each of its foreign keys, extracting parent key values and scanning the child table under an MVCC snapshot, followed by a 100-line dispatch matching Restrict, NoAction, Cascade, SetNull and SetDefault. The intermediate actions_to_perform tuple is already the seam between them.

hash_expression is a single exhaustive match over the ~40 variants of vibesql_ast::Expression, and every arm is variant-specific field enumeration (ColumnRef hashes table_canonical/column_canonical, Between hashes expr/low/high/negated/symmetric, MatchAgainst hashes columns then search_modifier then mode). There is no repeated scaffold to factor: the length is exactly the number of AST variants times the fields each one carries. Splitting it into hash_subquery/hash_temporal groups would force the outer arms to keep naming the variants and then re-match inside, and would give up the one place where the compiler's exhaustiveness check catches a newly added Expression variant.

eval_between opens with three dispatch prologues (row value constructor operands, scalar subquery against row-value bounds, the mixed row-value misuse check), then defines a 35-line transform_for_collation closure handling NOCASE and RTRIM over four SqlValue variants, then runs affinity resolution and the reversed-bounds and negation comparisons. The collation transform is a pure function that belongs beside the other collation helpers.

deserialize_value's bulk is mechanical boilerplate, not dispatch: the INTEGER, SMALLINT, BIGINT, UNSIGNED, NUMERIC, FLOAT, REAL and DOUBLE arms are eight copies of `let mut buf = [0u8; N]; reader.read_exact(&mut buf)?; Ok(...::from_le_bytes(buf))`, and CHARACTER/VARCHAR, INTERVAL, VECTOR and BLOB each re-spell the same `read u32 length, then read that many bytes` prologue. A `read_le::<N>(reader)` helper and a `read_len_prefixed(reader)` helper collapse those twelve arms to one or two lines each and take the function well under the bound, leaving the tag dispatch itself untouched. The DATE and TIMESTAMP arms, which carry the real logic (the from_parts_unchecked leniency comment), also stop being buried in byte plumbing.

try_extract_subqueries_to_joins carries two blocks of about 45 lines each, one for the left operand and one for the right of the And arm, that repeat the same In, Exists and scalar-comparison dispatch with only the sibling expression swapped, followed by two more symmetric recursive branches. One helper taking the candidate side and its remainder collapses all four.

The 2268 lines carry no test module at all: it is all production code, and it holds at least four independent concerns that already sit in contiguous runs. Table-reference discovery (collect_stmt_table_refs, collect_from_table_refs, collect_expr_table_refs at 724-1038 plus stmt_references_table, from_clause_references_table, expr_references_table at 2137-2268), wildcard expansion (WildcardColumn, WildcardSource, visible_columns, view_column_names, expand_wildcard_names, collect_from_sources, collect_select_list_columns at 1096-1371) and the recursive-CTE machinery (RecursiveSplit, split_recursive_compound, execute_recursive_cte, execute_recursive_frontier, execute_recursive_queue at 1371-1980) each move to a cte/refs.rs, cte/wildcard.rs and cte/recursive.rs with no signature change, leaving execute_ctes and execute_cte_at in the parent.

evaluate is a single 569-line match over Expression whose arms are fully independent: Cast recurses then calls cast_value, Between reimplements symmetric bound swapping and three-valued logic, InList runs its own NULL bookkeeping loop, and Like re-derives text coercion across the SqlValue variants. Each arm is 50 to 150 lines and depends only on its own sub-expressions, so one function per arm is the direct decomposition.

execute_with_iterators is already written as labeled stages and the seams are named in its own comments: the ExecutionContext assembly (outer_row/procedural/trigger/cte/outer_rows, ~25 lines), Stage 2's five-arm WhereOptimization match, Stage 3 and 4's OFFSET/LIMIT boxing, and Stage 6's SIMD-or-row-by-row projection (~40 lines). Each is a self-contained extraction over values it already computes (schema, evaluator, filtered_rows), for instance a build_evaluation_context(&self, &schema) -> Evaluator and a project_rows(&self, &filtered_rows, stmt, &evaluator, &schema). Nothing here is forced by a trait contract; the function is long because six pipeline stages were inlined into one body.

extract_column_refs is an exhaustive visitor over the Expression enum: every arm is one to three recursive calls, and the tail lists the terminal variants (Literal, Wildcard, CurrentDate, Placeholder and friends) explicitly with no wildcard arm. The length is set by the width of the AST, not by logic, and splitting the match would surrender the exhaustiveness check that forces every new variant to be handled.

The twelve arms of resolve_aliases_in_expression repeat one concrete scaffold: call resolve_alias_or_clone on each child, set an any_resolved flag, then rebuild the variant with unwrap_or_else(|| child.as_ref().clone()) on every unresolved child, else return None. Between spends 20 lines on three children, InList and Function spend 20 more each on the same flag-tracking closure, and Case spends 60. A single `fn resolve_child(child, select_list, any: &mut bool) -> Expression` returning the clone when nothing resolved reduces every one of those arms to a two- to five-line rebuild and removes the hand-written flag bookkeeping that is currently duplicated in five closures.

The file measures 1054 lines but production code stops at line 263: evaluate_arithmetic_simd, evaluate_binary_arithmetic_simd, apply_int64_op, apply_float64_op, get_numeric_column, create_literal_array, cast_to_float64 and cast_int64_to_float64, a cohesive and already small Arrow kernel wrapper. Lines 264 to 1054 are one `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` holding 24 independent `#[test]` functions that each build a RecordBatch and assert a kernel result. Keeping unit tests in an inline cfg(test) module beside the code they exercise is the idiomatic Rust form, and the only change the measurement asks for is relocating that module to a sibling file, which changes nothing about how the module is organized.

The single impl ArenaParser<'arena> mixes three unrelated layers: the public parse entry points and their _with_interner twins (parse_sql, parse_select, parse_insert/update/delete/replace and six mirrors), the statement dispatchers (parse_statement, parse_create_statement, parse_drop_statement), and a token-cursor toolkit of roughly twenty primitives (peek, peek_next, peek_at_offset, advance, peek_keyword, consume_keyword, try_consume_keyword, expect_keyword, expect_token, try_consume, expect_statement_end, next_placeholder). Rust allows a second `impl ArenaParser` in another file, and the module already splits its grammar across ddl, delete, expression, insert, select and update submodules, so moving the cursor primitives into arena_parser/cursor.rs follows the layout the crate itself established and costs no signature change.

parse_add_column holds a type and generated-clause prologue, a DEFAULT clause read twice for ordering, and then an 80-line constraint loop with six arms (NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY, UNIQUE, REFERENCES with optional column list, CHECK with verbatim source capture, DEFAULT). The comments in the CHECK and generated arms say they mirror create/table.rs and create/constraints.rs, so a shared column-constraint parser is the stated target.

parse_values_statement_internal is five sequential clause parsers inlined into one body: the set-operation tail (op keyword, ALL/DISTINCT, parenthesized or bare right side, ~50 lines), ORDER BY with its MAX_ORDER_BY_TERMS check (~35), the ORDER-BY-before-set-operation lookahead that saves and restores self.position (~28), LIMIT with comma syntax plus OFFSET (~30), and the valid_end_token match (~30). Each depends only on &mut self and the three boolean flags, so each extracts as its own method. parse_select_statement_internal sits at line 55 of the same file and parses the same trailing clauses, so the extraction is also the factoring that stops the two from drifting.

Cursor::execute is a 60-line prepare prologue (statement cache lookup, parameter substitution, parse, cache insert) followed by a match over ten Statement variants, where CreateTable, DropTable and the other schema changers each repeat the same statement-cache and schema-cache clearing block. Extracting prepare and the cache invalidation leaves a thin dispatch.

The impl Database at lines 124 to 1412 holds six separable families under one block: b-tree index CRUD and metadata (create_index through list_indexes_for_table), partial indexes (add_to_partial_indexes_for_insert through clear_partial_index_data), expression indexes (add_to_expression_indexes_for_insert through clear_expression_index_data), spatial indexes (create_spatial_index, get/drop/list_spatial_index*), vector indexes (create_ivfflat_index, search_ivfflat_index, set_ivfflat_probes, create_hnsw_index, search_hnsw_index, set_hnsw_ef_search), and the lookup and delete paths (lookup_by_index_* and a 165-line delete_by_pk_fast that is a row-deletion routine rather than index metadata). Database is already implemented across database/core.rs, database/operations.rs and this file, so splitting the vector and spatial groups into their own sibling files is the layout the crate already uses.

The HnswIndex impl runs 32 methods in four separable groups: parameter accessors, graph construction (build and a 110-line insert with select_neighbors and prune_neighbors), tombstone removal and compaction (unlink, should_compact, compact, thresholds, take_compacted), and query (search plus search_layer). The four distance functions (compute_distance, l2_distance, cosine_distance, inner_product_distance) touch no index state at all.

adjudication.sampling: Deterministic sample of up to 5 sites per rule. The population of a rule is the set of its corpus findings ordered canonically by (repository, path, line); sites sharing that identity are collapsed once. From a population of n such sites the sample takes k = min(5, n) of them, at the indices floor(i * n / k) for i in [0, k), a regular stride from the first site, so the sample follows the same distribution as the findings a user actually receives. Every sampled site was read in the pinned source with its surrounding code. The published rate is the rate of that sample, never of the unreviewed population; at k = 5 the sample resolves steps of 20 points, so it separates a rule with no observed false positive from one that has some, and cannot place a rule precisely against the 5 % threshold. Structural rules sample their production-context subpopulation, with the same stride: a family marked as a test, benchmark, example or build-script context does not weigh on the score, so the rate that decides what a structural rule costs is the rate of the families that do. rust_doctor::structure::duplicate_function_body samples k = min(20, n) of that subpopulation, because its published target is a rate at or under 5 percent and a five-site sample cannot resolve that threshold; the other structural rules sample five. The unit of a structural sample is the family or unit the diagnostic reports, read at its anchor together with its related sites. The all-context measurement of 2026-08-09, which this replaced, is recorded in docs/structural-precision-2026-08.md with its composition. Three rules were deepened on 2026-08-11, past the five-site default, because five sites resolve steps of twenty points and cannot place a rule against the threshold. clippy::indexing_slicing takes k = 40 of its 241 sites by the same stride, which contains the k = 5 stride it replaces. clippy::string_slice reviews its whole population of 40, so its rate is exact rather than sampled. rust_doctor::structure::complex_function reviews 31 of the 34 production families it observes. Every added site was judged twice by independent passes blind to each other, and the three sites where the passes disagreed are excluded from the sample and left to a human verdict rather than settled by the agent that produced them, which is why complex_function reviews 31 and not 34. The agreement of those passes is published per rule and population in adjudication.agreement.coefficients, which the suite recomputes from the pairs on record: no count and no coefficient is stated here, because a number written in prose is a number no test compares. The four structural rules of the agent population are drawn by that same stride over their production-context subpopulation, at the target their plan publishes, bounded by what the population can supply, with the population, the target and the positions the stride landed on recorded in adjudication.sampling_plan and the draw enrolled in adjudication.adjudicated_after_cutoff. That subpopulation is the findings the scan publishes with no context, and it excludes a finding under a tests, benches or examples directory or in a file named tests.rs even where the scan attributes no context to it: the correction of August 2026 to how a module declared out of line under a cfg(test) attribute is classified shrank all four populations, and one predicate now decides both what a rule is measured over and what the record may publish as a production site. A population that changes size does not keep its sample, since the stride recomputes every position from n, so each of the four plans names the positions of the sites an earlier plan drew that survived the correction, in adjudication.sampling_plan.carried_over. The carry-over extends the sample and never edits the draw: a carried position is a position of the corrected population that the new stride did not select, and the verdicts behind it are the verdicts already on record rather than a re-reading of the same site.

trigger_verification.method: Mechanical: the rule's trigger is searched inside the reported span at the pinned revision. This is a guard against corrupted spans only. It cannot measure precision, because the lint that looks for a pattern always finds that pattern.

agent_population.selection_criterion: A repository qualifies when at least half of the commit messages reachable from its pinned revision contain its recorded marker, an exact substring such as 'Co-Authored-By: Claude' or 'Generated with [Claude Code]' that coding agents append to the commits they author. The criterion reads the git history alone, never code style, README claims or popularity, and marked_commits and total_commits are recounted mechanically from git log at the pinned revision when the corpus is replayed. The population is scanned with every Clippy rule off, because its build scripts and proc-macros are untrusted: the native detectors parse source text and compile nothing.

trust_boundary.rationale: Cargo runs build scripts and procedural macros, so the Clippy leg of every corpus scan is an explicit trusted boundary: only mature, widely reviewed repositories are pinned. The native detectors parse source text and never compile or execute corpus code, which the harness proves by replaying the corpus with every Clippy rule switched off.
